canDo: Can relate journeys — leaving, arriving, coming back — and handle basic agreement.
review: Review D5; add aller/venir/partir/arriver/rentrer and similar verbs.
input: Listening: getting around on a trip; reading: a trip recap/a travel incident.
output: Write 90 words about a trip; speak for 90 seconds with at least 4 être verbs.
checkpoint: Can explain why être is used; aware of agreement with feminine/plural subjects.
challenge: Today’s challenge: think of your latest trip (even just to a nearby town) and write 6 sentences describing leaving, arriving and coming back, with at least 4 verbs that take être (partir, arriver, rester, rentrer…); then check the gender and number agreement of every past participle.

questions.why: marché is a Saturday activity; the departure time itself is not a problem.
« Léa est redescendue tout de suite »; the parents only arrived on Sunday.
mardi is the day of the return journey, vendredi the day of departure.
The ticket goes to Amboise; the train was going the right way — it was the station he got off at that was wrong.
« sans supplément » rules out paying extra; the inspector hadn’t come by yet.
The concluding sentence says the exact opposite of the third option.
The entorse is the only reason; « plus long » describes the way down.
« un autre chemin, plus long mais moins raide » is an explicit comparison.
« vingt minutes d'avance sur l'horaire annoncé » — note the difference between avance and retard.
« ce que je ne fais jamais le jeudi » is the key aside; Mme Ferrand had already moved back in the spring.
au printemps is when she moved back, not where she went after moving away.
« l'impression d'avoir retrouvé quelque chose » + planning to take the same way again.
« Non, en train » is a direct answer; the car is still at the garage.
He has to go back on Saturday, so he hasn’t picked it up yet.
« Il est complet, sauf l'attestation d'assurance » is the key information.
The text says délai plus long; it doesn’t say the application was refused.
It’s his colleague who is on leave, not Mme Roux.
Compare 410 (paying) with 200 (free); the last sentence points out the surprise.
« entièrement reversés » rules out any other use.
These thirty people are precisely the ones who did not take part in the walk.
She had an address and her luggage; the problem was with checking her documents.
« une amie d'amie » is a friend of a friend.
deux ans is how long she has been in France.
